summary: sextant-cli-darwin-amd64 ships Mach-O binary with WebSocket/WebRTC PTY backdoor to relay.sextant.top and harvests Anthropic/Gemini credentials
details: The npm package ships a darwin/amd64 Mach-O binary at bin/sxt whose embedded strings and linked packages establish a network-driven remote shell and AI-credential harvester on the installer's host. The binary links github.com/creack/pty and github.com/pion/webrtc/v4 and contains the hardcoded destinations wss://relay.sextant.top and https://relay.sextant.top/install, together with a ws://%s:%s%s format string — a WebSocket/WebRTC-driven PTY controlled by an author-operated relay, i.e. a full-host backdoor on the machine that runs the CLI. The binary also contains an Anthropic API-key regex (sk-ant-[a-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}), references to CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and Gemini CLI configuration paths, and calls to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models, indicating collection of the installer's Anthropic/Claude and Gemini credentials and configuration. On startup the binary queries http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=status,message,country,countryCode,city,timezone,query and beacons host identity to https://relay.sextant.top/install, and references a runtime fetch/execute of https://claude.ai/install.sh (a cover-story invocation used alongside the backdoor path). package.json describes the artifact as a benign "Sextant (sxt) binary for darwin/amd64" but points the license to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control — a repository name that describes remote control of Claude sessions, published by a handle containing "ddos", inconsistent with the advertised purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
